## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: NONE (low confidence in any specific commit; see reasoning)

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach.** I read the full diff of the supplied "fix" commit (a1f90f01) hunk by hunk and classified each change as either a pure type-safety/generics refactor (raw type → parameterized type, `Iterator`/`while` → for-each) or an actual behavioral change. I then used `git log --follow` and `git show` on the touched files (`CallLocalityContext.java`, `ClassInfoFlowAnalysis.java`, `ClassLocalObjectsAnalysis.java`, `InfoFlowAnalysis.java`, `SimpleMethodInfoFlowAnalysis.java`, `DominatorNode.java`, `DominatorTree.java`, `MHGDominatorTree.java`) to see where the underlying classes had previously changed shape, since a1f90f01 is dated the same day as, and immediately follows, merge commit `51e7abd7` (which brought in `14ec743b`, a large commit by a different author that converted `DominatorNode`, `DominatorTree`, `MHGDominatorTree`, and parts of the info-flow classes to use Java generics).

**(2) What I found in a1f90f01.** Essentially every hunk is mechanical:
- `CallLocalityContext`: `List<Object>` → `List<EquivalentValue>`, plus removal of dead/unused local variables (`List ret = new ArrayList();`, `ThisRef thisRef`).
- `ClassInfoFlowAnalysis`/`InfoFlowAnalysis`/`SimpleMethodInfoFlowAnalysis`: raw `HashMutableDirectedGraph`/`FlowSet`/`Pair` → their already-generic counterparts (`HashMutableDirectedGraph<EquivalentValue>`, etc.), and manual `Iterator` loops rewritten as for-each loops. I verified `HashMutableDirectedGraph<N>`, `DirectedGraph<N>`, and `MutableDirectedGraph<N>` were *already* generic classes long before this commit and before `14ec743b` — the info-flow code (authored in 2007, per its header comment) had simply never adopted the generic signatures, so using it as a raw type never caused a runtime defect (type erasure means the actual objects were always `EquivalentValue`s).
- `TestDominance.java`: updated to use `DominatorNode<Node>`/`DominatorTree<Node>` instead of raw types + casts, catching up with `14ec743b`'s generics change to those classes. Raw usage would still have compiled (with unchecked warnings) so this wasn't fixing a build break either.
- The one place with an actual logic difference is the debug-only `printInfoFlowSummary` method (`if(!nodeIt.hasNext())` → `if(g.size() > 0)`, and a `sourcesIt.hasNext()`-style check replaced with an off-by-one `idx` counter). These are purely cosmetic console-output helpers with no test coverage, and if anything this commit *introduces* a minor formatting inconsistency here rather than fixing one — it isn't a plausible candidate for "the bug" in an SZZ sense.

**(3) Conclusion / evidence.** I could not find any hunk in a1f90f01 that corrects an actual behavioral defect (wrong computation result, crash, `ClassCastException`, etc.). Every substantive change is either (a) applying pre-existing generic APIs to code that had always used them raw without ill effect, or (b) catching test code up to a generics change (`14ec743b`) that itself was also a non-behavioral refactor. Since Java raw-type usage of an already-generic class produces only compiler warnings, not runtime bugs, there is no code state before a1f90f01 that can be shown to have been functionally broken by an identifiable prior commit.

Given this, I don't have solid evidence to name a specific bug-introducing commit. The only remotely related predecessor is `14ec743b` (merged as `51e7abd7`), which started the generics migration that a1f90f01 completes for the remaining files — but I found no proof that `14ec743b` caused any actual runtime misbehavior, only inconsistency in code style. I'm reporting `BIC: NONE` to reflect this honestly rather than assert a causal link I can't substantiate.
